answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a canyon as the anchor of the cost.
